This supersedes the C17 language/build lock and the former two-implementation-worker ceiling. Use as many useful disjoint Luna codex exec workers as available allowance/resources permit; preserve one writer per module and coordinator-only shared integration. # Agent rules

Read [OWNER-DIRECTIVES.md](OWNER-DIRECTIVES.md) first. It overrides conflicting
roadmap and tooling text. Follow the active `work/WO-*.md`; inspect its allowed
and protected paths before editing. Keep each work order buildable, tested,
verified, and recorded in `STATE.md` and the ledgers.

## Platform and product locks

- Initial support is Apple Silicon macOS 13+. Do not add Linux/Windows code,
  shims, CI jobs, runners, packaging, or portability work.
- Keep platform implementations behind `platform/` interfaces; do not add
  stubs for unsupported operating systems.
- Rust for all first-party code is the active owner-approved migration target.
  MPL-2.0, minimal pinned dependencies, custom-drawn UI, and an owned SVG
  parser/rasterizer remain locked. Legacy C17 code is preserved as migration
  reference; do not resume old C implementation orders. See ADR-0022.
- Never read, fetch, or copy GPL SVG-editor source. Do not fetch external SVG
  resources from the application. Record provenance for external algorithms.

## Repository map

- `app/`: executable composition.
- `src/`: base, platform, XML/SVG, scene, raster, document, UI modules as added.
- `docs/research-r4/`: authoritative operating model and roadmap.
- `docs/research-r3/plan/`: architecture and coding guidance where r4 is silent.
- `docs/adr/`: accepted decisions; `work/`: immutable ready work orders.
- `tests/`: unit, property, fuzz, UI, and oracle tests as introduced.
- `bench/`: corpus metadata, generators, runners, and results.
- `artifacts/`: work-order evidence; `build/` and `.cache/` are generated.

## Commands

The commands below are the preserved legacy C workflow. Rust workspace/build
commands become authoritative only through their implementation orders.

- `./dev build`: configure and build Debug.
- `./dev test-fast`: run local Python tests and validate the ledger.
- `./dev verify`: run the Debug build and fast tests.
- `cmake --preset mac-release && cmake --build --preset mac-release`: Release.
- `python3 scripts/ledger.py validate ledger.jsonl`: validate work history.
- `python3 -m unittest`: run Python harness tests when present.
- `bench`, `fmt`, `lint`, `asan`, and `fuzz` become authoritative only when
  their work orders implement them; do not claim missing commands run.

## Engineering and safety

Use the contracts in `docs/CODING_STANDARD.md`: explicit ownership, pointer+length
slices, checked size arithmetic, bounded user input, no VLAs, and no unsafe
string functions. Preserve unknown SVG/XML source. Keep generated files in
ignored repo-local directories. Do not install system packages or touch sibling
directories. Add dependencies only through an ADR and pinned provenance record.

Never weaken frozen acceptance tests or oracles. Run commands named by the
active work order, then report exact evidence. Do not invent test or performance
results. Keep source files focused and under 800 lines; split cohesive modules
before they grow further.

## Rust migration execution

Follow `docs/product/rust-port-goal-and-plan.md` and ready Rust work orders.
Multiple Luna codex exec processes are authorized, with isolated current-source
worktrees and disjoint modules; coordinator alone changes shared manifests,
locks, interfaces and ledgers. Use Low for inventory/docs, Medium for routine
ports, High for parser/renderer/concurrency/unsafe FFI. Escalate only on a named
problem; use the existing subscription allowance and no purchased credits.
Preserve strict validation, original fixtures/assertions and byte-preserving
round trips. Rust ownership replaces manual C ownership conventions; bounded
inputs, checked arithmetic, safe cleanup and source limits still apply. Keep

# ADR0026: pinned Apple bindings and contained ABI failures

Status: Proposed for focused review, then accepted only by the coordinator.
Date:2026-10-14. Work order:WO-RUST-NATIVE-BINDINGS-SETUP-01.

## Decision

Use the exact16package closure and default-disabled native feature selection in
`docs/dependencies/objc2-macos.lock.json`, derived from the accepted native audit.
Add Foundation NSException for genuine exception-boundary probes/diagnostics;
no package is added. Application/platform implementations remain first-party
Rust. Generated Apple bindings and the small upstream Objective-C exception
helper are reviewed third-party FFI dependencies, not a first-party backend shim.
The owned SVG/XML/raster and custom UI locks remain unchanged. No dispatch,
GNUstep, static-class/selector macros or unsupported-OS application work.

Keep AppKit-facing owners !Send/!Sync with an acquired main-thread capability.
Native pointers remain private to platform implementation. Callbacks enqueue
bounded owned data without model mutation/reentrancy or retained borrowed inputs.

The enforceable ABI contract is: no Rust panic or Objective-C exception escapes
a platform public operation or an inbound Objective-C/C/block callback. objc2
catch-all uses its pinned helper's explicit C-unwind trampoline and native catch
fence, then converts message exceptions to Rust panics. This audited dependency
mechanism is allowed inside the platform boundary; the prior proposal's absolute
zero-foreign-unwind-at-any-Rust-frame wording is superseded. Use Rust guards at
public platform operations and inside each inbound callback; latch owned bounded
faults and return ABI-valid fallback. No application-model/RefCell borrow may
span a native call that can reenter callbacks. Runtime source inspection, real
exception/panic probes and subsequent per-callback reviews remain necessary.

Raw C/CF APIs, retain/release/Drop and foreign exception cleanup are not all
fenced by catch-all. Rely only on their published validated ownership/argument
contracts; do not advertise recovery from corrupted objects or unsupported
cleanup exceptions. Panic=abort/allocator abort cannot recover; supported guards
use unwind. No manual objc_msgSend/transmute, fabricated main-thread marker,
foreign-unwind bypass or C shim is allowed.

## Provenance and licensing

Published registry checksums/manifests/selected APIs and exact VCS license
overviews are retained. Canonical MIT/Apache2/Zlib grants linked by those
overviews are retained, not invented copyright attribution. Select MIT where
the published package permits it; preserve all upstream notices and declared
authors with exact-version links in release attribution. Published build tools
include their own MIT/Apache notices. Apple SDK derivation and installed SDK27
provenance are recorded; this decision is no legal-clearance claim, no SDK/source
redistribution approval, and no acceptance of another agreement on the owner's
behalf. Release notice assembly and distribution review remain release gates.
Local use of the existing SDK is unchanged; no system packages are installed.

## Evidence required

Independent focused review before adoption. Exact-lock16package graph and
feature/host-target resolution, compiler1.99/mac13 deployment, offline build,
real Foundation exception handling, Rust panic/success, mainthread denial and
opaque/thread-confined API checks. Newer APIs require explicit availability
checks; current-host success alone cannot establish macOS13 runtime support.
Native shell/IME/text/media/GPU/menu/AX/teardown and final application acceptance
are separate complete work orders. Dependencies neither replace owned vector
logic nor prove performance improvements.

## Ownership, thread and foreign boundaries

Published `MainThreadMarker::new() -> Option<Self>` uses Apple's
`pthread_main_np`; its marker is `!Send + !Sync`. NSApplication inherits the
main-thread responder boundary. Acquire the capability safely; do not use
`new_unchecked` to bypass it. Keep application/window/menu/AX/preferences/
presenter owners main-thread confined even where framework types are permissive.

`Retained<T>` retains/releases Objective-C ownership; `CFRetained<T>` owns CF
Create results. Get-returned objects remain borrowed or must be retained before
escaping. Platform wrappers expose no native pointers. Delegates/observers/
blocks route by invalidatable window generation. Callbacks copy bounded owned
UTF-8/path events, never retain model/pixel borrows or mutate the model
reentrantly. Preserve the 256-event queue/fault policy, accepted scale limits,
text/glyph/path/cache bounds and checked RGBA sizes. IME requires complete
NSTextInputClient requirements and UTF-16 range conversion; legacy
charactersIgnoringModifiers is insufficient.

Block2 is justified by asynchronous sheets, notification/timer observers and
MTLCommandBuffer completion. `RcBlock::new` copies captures to heap; clone uses
_Block_copy. Heap copying does not extend borrowed captures. Use owned captures
and explicit lifetime/invalidation. Published blocks do not enforce every
cross-thread capture condition: Metal completion captures must be thread-safe,
without UI markers or model borrows. Completion only updates bounded retained
submission state; main-thread UI observes owned results. CGPathApply needs no
block. Copy frame bytes before returning; retain in-flight GPU resources, tolerate
missing drawables, and separate readback verification.

Rust panic handling and Objective-C exceptions are distinct. Published objc2
`catch-all` activates `exception`, wrapping message sends and converting caught
Objective-C exceptions to Rust panics. Explicit `exception::catch` returns an
exception result while Rust panics continue. Both require the published helper:
its build.rs uses cc/Clang, `-xobjective-c`, `-fobjc-exceptions`, without ARC;
`try_catch.m` catches Objective-C objects, retains them and lets Rust/C++ unwinds
continue. This is third-party Objective-C, not an authorized first-party shim.
Adoption must explicitly accept this native build dependency and audit its
complete provenance/closure. No pure-Rust foreign-exception fence is established.

Catch Rust unwinds inside every inbound callback, latch failure and return an
ABI-valid fallback; never unwind into AppKit/C/block callers. Panic=abort cannot
provide recovery. Catch-all is not a guarantee against exceptions from raw C
calls, retain/release, cleanup or exceptional exception handling, and the helper
uses a Rust C-unwind trampoline internally. The proposal's absolute prohibition
on foreign unwinding through Rust therefore needs an explicit boundary decision;
catch_unwind alone cannot satisfy it. Legacy KVO @try/@catch cannot simply be
removed. Teardown invalidates routing, cancels sheets/timers, unregisters
observers, detaches delegates and retires GPU resources before object release.
